Job Description

Role Overview:

The team
Citadel Securities is one of the largest market makers in the world, providing liquidity across nearly every major asset class and market globally, in real time. Machine learning is fundamental to how we do it.

We are the firm’s centralized applied-AI team, working with strategy teams across the firm. We conduct the frontier model research that benefits all of them in common — the deep-learning models that predict where prices are going — and we tailor that research to the highest-impact strategies. We build the systems that turn those predictions into trading decisions, as well as the tooling that enables researchers across the firm to apply machine learning to their own problems. As the centralized team, we take on the hardest applied-AI problems first and set the standard the wider organization follows. Our research is applied: it ships to production and is measured by its impact on the business.

Every member of the team is a member of technical staff — a strong generalist with depth in at least one specialty, whether deep learning, large-scale ML systems, applied LLMs and agents, or the mechanics of markets themselves. We operate in small teams with end-to-end ownership and minimal bureaucracy.

The role
You build ML applications and systems that move real money, and you want to understand why they work — not simply ship them. You write code once you understand the research context and why it matters, and you are equally comfortable reading a research paper and profiling a training run.

As Quantitative AI Technical Staff, you will have substantial independence to pursue the research directions you believe are most impactful, supported by state-of-the-art clusters with a very high compute-to-researcher ratio and by dedicated engineering, hardware, and systems teams that help bring your ideas into production. You will be responsible for improving every part of our models — from how we featurize raw market data, to architecture design, to training dynamics, to how a model’s predictions become trading decisions. The role is approximately half research and half engineering.

Your work will be directly and measurably impactful on the business, and it will be challenging: this is a field with no easy or obvious solutions.

Prior experience in finance or markets is not required. Many of us joined without it; we hire for ability, curiosity, and growth trajectory, and we will teach you the markets. This is an entry-level role, and we welcome candidates whose qualifications align with the position.

How we work
We work in an AI-native way. Directing several coding agents in parallel — to run experiment sweeps, refactor subsystems, or investigate issues across a large codebase — is a normal part of the workflow, and we expect everyone to develop fluency in it.

We hold ourselves to a high standard of scientific rigor. Because our results translate directly into capital at risk, sound research methodology is essential: forming clear, testable hypotheses; designing controlled and reproducible experiments; comparing approaches on a consistent, like-for-like basis; and carefully distinguishing genuine signal from noise or overfitting. We value researchers who are skeptical of their own results and who validate their conclusions before acting on them.

The systems we work with are complex, and understanding them well is part of the job. Clear communication matters: we collaborate continuously with quantitative researchers and traders across a large organization.

Responsibilities:

Model research. Design and train the deep-learning models that predict where prices are going — developing new architectures, improving features, and extending how far into the future the models can reliably predict.
Enabling ML across the firm. Build the systems and tooling that allow many other researchers to apply machine learning to their own problems, multiplying your impact well beyond your own work.
High-impact markets. Take on novel problems in markets that generate billions of dollars in annual revenue, where established solutions do not yet exist.
From prediction to trading decisions. A prediction is only useful once it informs a decision to buy or sell. We apply AI across the full chain — including simulating how a set of trades would perform before any capital is committed, and a growing range of decision problems beyond prediction itself.

What makes it challenging
The problems are difficult and genuinely adversarial: predicting price movements from the fine-grained patterns in how millions of orders arrive and change, extending those predictions further into the future, simulating trading outcomes accurately, and building infrastructure that supports many distinct trading strategies at once. Unlike most AI work, which is evaluated on benchmarks, our work is evaluated by the market — a demanding, high-stakes environment with immediate feedback. The quality of your work is reflected directly and quickly in measurable financial outcomes.

Qualifications:

Have strong software engineering fundamentals and write clean, efficient, correct code.
Have solid depth in machine learning and deep learning, with hands-on experience training and debugging models.
Are results-oriented, with a bias toward action, flexibility, and efficiency.
Are genuinely curious about how markets work and why trades are profitable, even without a prior finance background.
Communicate clearly and collaborate effectively across a large, technical organization (this role involves substantial collaboration).
Are coachable and respond well to feedback; we value growth trajectory over starting point.
Are comfortable working in an AI-native way, directing multiple agents to carry out research and engineering, or are eager to learn.

Strong candidates may also have experience with
(None of the following is required, but any of it is a real plus.)

Building applications with LLM agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, or custom frameworks) at meaningful scale.
Transformer architectures and modern foundation models; post-training techniques such as supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or preference optimization.
High-performance or large-scale ML systems; GPUs/TPUs; JAX or PyTorch.
Large-scale data pipelines and distributed training.
A demonstrated record of excellence in a demanding area — for example, competitive programming, mathematics or physics olympiads, Kaggle, significant open-source contributions, or research publications.

Basics

Education: Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD — or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience — in a relevant field (computer science, mathematics, physics, electrical engineering, statistics, or similar).
Experience: Entry-level; graduates across all degree levels are encouraged to apply. Required experience will correspond to the internal level of the position.

The Firm

XTX Markets is a leading algorithmic trading firm. We build models that forecast prices for more than 53,000 financial instruments across equities, fixed income, currencies, commodities and crypto. Those forecasts are used to trade on exchanges and other venues and provide liquidity to clients worldwide. The firm trades over $250bn a day across 35 countries and has over 300 employees in London, Singapore, New York, Paris, Bristol, Mumbai, Yerevan and Kajaani.

XTX is a technology business. Trading is driven by research, large-scale computation and careful engineering. Over the last decade, our trading models have evolved from the econometric methods that gave the firm its name, through trees and neural networks, to modern deep learning architectures. We expect that evolution to continue.

XTX has an unusually large research platform for a trading firm, with well over 25,000 GPUs and more than 1 exabyte of usable storage, alongside further compute being built in Finland. The aim is simple: good ideas and decisions should not be bottlenecked by data, infrastructure or compute.

At XTX Markets, technology is our business. We are a diverse organisation that attracts outstanding talent from across all industry backgrounds. Our people collaborate across the business, working openly and respectfully with each other, our clients and the market. Our culture is non-hierarchical, everyone is valued, and we strive for excellence in everything we do.

The Role

The Trading Desk is the real-time control layer for XTX’s automated trading businesses, working with quantitative research, trading technology, risk, operations, exchanges and clients to keep the engine operating reliably 24/7.

As a Trading Desk Analyst, you will take operational ownership of this layer. The role requires deep systems thinking rather than software engineering, and a strong grasp of the principles, inputs, outputs and failure modes of our automated trading infrastructure.

In this role, you will use internal tools, dashboards and automated workflows to monitor, diagnose and optimize real-time engine performance. When anomalies arise, you will interrogate the data quickly and execute or coordinate interventions to safeguard firm, client and counterparty capital. You will translate complex operational signals into high-impact decisions that prevent losses and drive measurable value.

This role is for a highly curious, analytical thinker who thrives under pressure and wants direct responsibility for a multi-billion dollar trading engine. We are looking for someone with an ownership mindset on every shift, who proactively prevents losses and improves system outcomes.

Responsibilities

As a member of the desk, your responsibilities include:

  • Real-Time Supervision: Own real-time supervision of automated trading strategies and related operations, focused on the markets most relevant to XTX.
  • System Intuition & Vigilance: Develop a strong understanding of expected engine behaviour. Maintain a healthy, proactive scepticism of automated outputs, hunting for irregularities and taking timely action before issues escalate.
  • Metrics & Analytics: Use trading metrics, dashboards, alerts and data workflows to understand performance, liquidity, execution quality, risk, positions and operational health.
  • Incident Response: Respond calmly and decisively to market events, venue issues, client flow, risk-limit changes and internal anomalies, escalating when required.
  • Incident Ownership: Own system alerts, anomalies and operational breaks from detection through resolution, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks.
  • Feedback Loop: Provide precise, evidence-based feedback to quantitative research and trading technology teams, turning live-market observations into useful questions and improvements.
  • Tool Development Partnership: Partner with researchers, developers and systems engineers to enhance monitoring and control tools; define what tools should show and how they should be used, rather than writing code for its own sake.
  • Knowledge Transfer: Maintain clear handovers and post-event notes so judgement, context and lessons learned compound over time, helping the global desk improve and avoid repeat incidents.
  • Shift Flexibility: Cover relevant APAC market hours, including scheduled shift work and occasional weekend coverage.

About You

Someone who is a good fit will resonate with most, if not all the following:

  • A genuine interest in automated trading, price forecasting, market structure, suboptimal signals and noisy data, with a passion for interrogating complex systems to find operational irregularities and failure modes.
  • Strong quantitative reasoning and practical trading intuition; able to form hypotheses, read ambiguous evidence, change your mind quickly and distinguish signal from noise.
  • The ability to operate a complex system without knowing every line of code or modelling detail, while learning enough of the principles to make sound decisions.
  • Strong judgement in uncertain conditions where the right action may not be obvious and the cost of delay or inaction can be meaningful.
  • Absolute ownership, accountability and commitment. We want someone who treats the engine’s behaviour as their responsibility, not someone seeking a passive monitoring role.
  • Very comfortable using data, dashboards and internal tools to diagnose problems and improve outcomes. Basic technical literacy is expected for navigating our data structures.
  • Precise written and verbal communication skills, especially when explaining messy live issues to researchers, engineers, risk managers, operations teams and senior stakeholders.
  • Integrity, intellectual honesty and high standards. XTX is a flat environment where ideas are challenged directly, and evidence matters more than hierarchy.

Essential Attributes

  • At least 5 years’ experience on a highly automated trading desk, in electronic market making, trading operations, risk, market structure or another high-accountability operational environment. Knowledge of FX, equities, futures, commodities or crypto markets is most beneficial.
  • A strong academic background in a quantitative discipline such as Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Physics, Engineering or a related field.
  • Functional proficiency with Python, Pandas and SQL. We value candidates who use these tools to parse data, audit anomalies and optimize desk workflows. Note: This is an infrastructure mastery role, not an incubator for algorithmic strategy design.
  • Experience making decisions from incomplete or noisy data in a fast-moving environment.
  • A track record of being exceptionally conscientious and reliable, with a desire to optimize processes over time.

PLEASE NOTE THAT EMPLOYEES OF XTX MAY NOT ENGAGE IN DAY-TRADING. YOU MAY BUY AND HOLD SECURITIES, CRYPTO AND OTHER ASSETS BUT YOU MUST HOLD EACH POSITION FOR AT LEAST 30 DAYS AFTER PURCHASE, REGARDLESS OF PRICE FLUCTUATION.

About the Position

We're looking for Linux Engineers to join the team that maintains the critical infrastructure underlying the rest of Jane Street's technology. It's a broad role, and no two Linux Engineers look exactly alike. Our work spans on-prem and cloud infrastructure, every major pillar (compute, storage, networking), and every layer of the stack from the physical hardware to workload orchestration. You should expect to work in some (but not necessarily all) of these areas, and to go genuinely deep in a few.

That might mean:

  • Building the in-house tools and systems that make up our platform, or integrating mainstream (often open-source) technologies so they feel native to our infrastructure
  • Acting as one of the firm's Linux experts, and teaching other engineers specialist skills like systems debugging
  • Automating our own work, because it makes us faster and more reliable (and we think it's fun)
  • Diagnosing and resolving production issues in real time, often under time pressure
  • Carrying out scheduled changes to the platform, like upgrades, migrations, capacity changes, and rollouts, planned meticulously and executed carefully

The problem space runs from the physical to the abstract: datacenter provisioning and orchestration, kernels and drivers delivered through Nix and RPMs, production and research storage at scale, cloud that integrates cleanly with our on-prem platform, and, in partnership with our IT and Network Engineering colleagues, Linux desktops and how our hosts participate in the network.

We see Linux Engineering and Software Engineering as two ends of a spectrum, and plenty of people could do either job well. Linux Engineering is likely the better fit if you treat Linux itself as your problem space: you like working close to the operating system, you want to look after production infrastructure, and you're happy spending more of your time in a consulting capacity than a typical developer would. (Compared with kernel development, the emphasis flips: you'd rarely develop the kernel itself, though targeted patches happen, and you'd spend far more time running production infrastructure.) We're hiring for both roles and are happy to advise you on which might fit best.

We don't expect you to come in with deep experience; we're happy to hire smart problem-solvers and teach them what they need to know. But the job leans much more toward engineering than a traditional operations role: relentless automation instead of manual toil, and a large body of in-house technology rather than only off-the-shelf tools. You'll build systems, not just operate them.

About You

We don't expect you to have a background in finance or any other specific field - we're looking for smart people who enjoy solving interesting problems. We're more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:

  • Knowledgeable about operating system fundamentals, computer architecture, and systems programming concepts like sockets, virtual memory, and the process life cycle
  • Able to understand network protocols at a basic level
  • Comfortable at the command line of a Linux machine (whether from coursework, side projects, or time spent administering a campus computer lab) and fluent in basic introspection and troubleshooting: system health, individual processes, logs
  • Someone who solves problems by writing code (in any language) and cares about robust software engineering
  • Intellectually curious, collaborative, humble, and eager to learn (including from mistakes)
  • A strong communicator
  • Fluent in English 

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

As a Lead Developer, you will own and evolve the core platform services that power our AI-driven products. You will work closely with AI engineers, front-end developers, and product stakeholders to translate investment use cases into robust back-end solutions.

  • Design, develop, and maintain back-end services and REST APIs using Python and FastAPI, serving both internal and external consumers.
  • Build and optimise LLM-based pipelines for information extraction, summarisation, and classification across diverse source types.
  • Develop and maintain agentic AI workflows using LangGraph, including tool orchestration, multi-step reasoning chains, and feedback loops.

  • LLM & AI Development: At least 1 year of hands-on experience building LLM-based applications, including one or more of: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agent-based systems (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph), LLM-driven data extraction, or prompt engineering.

Implement governance capabilities end-to-end, including Unity Catalog access controls, column-level security, data classification, lineage, and data quality standards

Track record of architectural ownership and designing end-to-end data solutions

Deep experience with Databricks, Lakehouse architectures, or comparable modern data technologies, including Delta table design, Unity Catalog governance, compute trade-offs, and downstream BI or AI workloads

LevelExperiencedLocationSydneyDepartmentTechnologyApplyApply
WHO WE ARE
Optiver is a global market maker founded in Amsterdam, with offices in London, Chicago, Austin, New York, Sydney, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Singapore, Taipei and Mumbai. Established in 1986, today we are a leading liquidity provider, with close to 2,000 employees in offices around the world, united in our commitment to improve the market through competitive pricing, execution and risk management. By providing liquidity on multiple exchanges across the world in various financial instruments we participate in the safeguarding of healthy and efficient markets. We provide liquidity to financial markets using our own capital, at our own risk, trading a wide range of products: listed derivatives, cash equities, ETFs, bonds and foreign currencies.
Optiver’s Sydney office is one of the primary players within Asian markets, trading a range of products. Established in 1996, we're an active participant on the Hong Kong, Korea, Singapore, Taiwan and Japan exchanges, and act as Optiver’s APAC head office.WHAT YOU'LL DO
We are looking for a Head of Observability Platform to lead observability as a business-critical platform capability across our globally distributed trading environment.
Observability at Optiver has evolved across multiple teams, regions, systems, and platforms. We have a capable but heterogeneous foundation across logs, metrics, telemetry pipelines, dashboards, alerting, and production diagnostics. We have formed a dedicated team to advance observability as a standalone platform capability: globally consistent, easy to adopt, reliable at scale, and deeply embedded in how Optiver builds, operates, diagnoses, and improves production systems.
As Head of Observability Platform, you will own the strategy, architecture, operating model, adoption approach, and roadmap for Optiver’s shared observability platform. The platform enables engineers, operators, trading teams, automated systems, and future agent-based workflows to collect, query, understand, and act on metrics, logs, traces, events, alerts, and health signals across Optiver’s global environment.
This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will not be the primary implementer of every system, but you will need the depth to challenge designs, guide architectural trade-offs, unblock engineers, and make high-quality decisions. You will lead a globally distributed team of engineers, partner closely with engineering stakeholders, and shape the standards, tooling, and practices that make observability effective at scale.
Your goal is to transform observability into a globally consistent, regionally federated platform capability. Your work will improve production diagnosis, reduce operational risk, increase platform resilience, improve developer experience, and strengthen confidence in Optiver’s trading systems.
In this role, you will:
Set the global strategy, architecture, operating model, and roadmap for Optiver’s observability platform.
Lead and develop a globally distributed team of engineers, shaping team mandate, ways of working, and capability.
Define what “good observability” means at Optiver, including expectations for telemetry quality, instrumentation, alerting, dashboards, service health, and diagnostic workflows.
Guide technical direction across telemetry collection, ingestion, storage, query, visualization, alerting, eventing, automation, and platform reliability.
Improve the reliability, scalability, performance, and cost-effectiveness of the platform as adoption and telemetry volumes grow.
Improve developer and operator experience through self-service workflows, golden paths, documentation, reusable patterns, APIs, dashboards, and investigation tooling.
Partner with engineering teams to drive adoption.
WHAT YOU'LL BRING You are an experienced technical leader who combines platform strategy, architectural judgement, people leadership, and delivery discipline. You are comfortable setting long-term direction while engaging deeply enough to challenge designs, make trade-offs, and help teams execute.
You understand that observability is not just a tooling problem. It is a platform, standards, reliability, developer experience, and adoption problem. You know how to build systems that engineers trust, operators can rely on, and the business can depend on during high-pressure production situations.
You will bring:
Proven experience leading engineering, SRE, platform, infrastructure, or observability teams in a complex technical environment.
Experience owning or shaping a platform capability, including strategy, roadmap, architecture, operating model, adoption, governance, and measurable outcomes.
Deep understanding of modern observability practices across logs, metrics, traces, events, alerting, dashboards, telemetry pipelines, diagnostics, instrumentation quality, and service health.
Experience designing or leading large-scale observability platforms, including ingest pipelines, storage backends, query systems, retention models, visualization, alerting, resilience, and scale-related trade-offs.
Strong technical judgement, people leadership, and delivery discipline.
Ability to influence without direct control across engineering teams.
A pragmatic approach to platform adoption, balancing global standardisation with regional autonomy, local production needs, and existing systems.
WHAT YOU'LL GET:
A performance-based bonus structure unmatched anywhere in the industry. We combine our profits across desks, teams and offices into a global profit pool, fostering a truly collaborative environment.
The chance to work alongside diverse and intelligent peers in a rewarding environment.
Training, mentorship and personal development opportunities.
Daily breakfast, lunch and an in-house barista.
Gym membership plus weekly in-house chair massages.
Regular social events, including a company trip every two years.
Guided relocation, a competitive relocation package and visa sponsorship where necessary.
DIVERSITY STATEMENT
Optiver is committed to diversity and inclusion. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, and welcome requests for reasonable adjustments during the process.
Questions? Get in touch with the recruitment team at careers@optiver.com.au.

Job Overview

We are seeking an experienced Engineer to join our Trading Systems team within the Front Office Systems group. This role is ideal for a hands-on engineer who can design, build, and support critical applications used by traders, portfolio managers, and investment teams.

The role builds on the core Trading Systems responsibilities of developing applications, backend services, APIs, cloud-based solutions, and integrations that support front-office trading and investment workflows. The successful candidate will be expected to operate with limited day-to-day supervision, apply sound technical judgment, influence technology decisions, mentor junior colleagues, and independently drive projects to completion.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, test, deploy, and support Trading Systems services, APIs, and workflow applications.

  • Build and maintain backend services using Python and C#.

  • Contribute to modern web applications using React, JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML, and CSS.

  • Develop and support cloud-based solutions using AWS services such as EKS, Lambda, EC2, S3, and RDS.

  • Partner with traders, portfolio managers, operations teams, and business stakeholders to translate workflow needs into technical solutions.

  • Support integrations with internal systems, OMS/EMS platforms, market data providers, trading platforms, and operational tools.

  • Improve workflows related to order lifecycle management, trading, execution, allocations, and post-trade processes.

  • Troubleshoot production issues, perform root-cause analysis, and implement durable fixes.

  • Contribute to technical design decisions, architecture discussions, code reviews, testing, release processes, and engineering best practices.

  • Identify opportunities to improve system reliability, performance, scalability, automation, and developer productivity.

  • Explore and apply Generative AI / LLM-based capabilities where they can improve workflows, automation, or user experience.

  • Mentor junior engineers and provide technical leadership within the team.

Requirements

  • Strong professional software engineering experience, preferably in financial services, fintech, asset management, or another business-critical technology environment.

  • Experience with object-oriented programming, preferably in Python or .NET.

  • Experience building backend services, APIs, application integrations, or data-driven systems.

  • Familiarity with AWS cloud services, including EKS, Lambda, EC2, S3, RDS, or similar services.

  • Experience with modern web development, preferably React and JavaScript/TypeScript.

  • Strong understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including APIs, data structures, version control, automated testing, debugging, and secure development practices.

  • Experience with relational databases and SQL.

  • Ability to independently deliver high-quality technical work with limited day-to-day supervision.

  • Ensuring efficient deployment of the latest models across a range of GPU architectures, adapting the inference stack as hardware evolves

  • Developing reference implementations, libraries and tooling to improve the efficiency and reliability of NLP workloads
  • Collaborating with researchers, senior stakeholders and engineers to design optimised solutions
  • Working with systems, architecture and platform teams to evolve the compute stack and influence long-term platform decisions

  • Proven experience profiling, benchmarking and optimising large-scale LLM inference workloads

We are looking for an experienced FP&A Manager to join Susquehanna’s FP&A team, based in Bala Cynwyd, PA. This is a player-coach role: you will own and execute day-to-day FP&A responsibilities while also helping build out the capabilities, processes, and tools the function needs as the firm grows.

 

The role spans financial planning, cost reporting, management reporting, and expense methodologies. There is meaningful work across all of these areas, and we need someone who can move fluidly between strategic thinking and hands-on execution. The right candidate is analytically sharp, a strong communicator, and genuinely energized by environments where the work is not yet fully defined. Experience in financial services or trading is a plus; familiarity with how a prop trading firm operates is a real differentiator. Yearly travel to our international offices may be required.

 

What You’ll Do

 

Planning & Forecasting

  • Own the firms budgeting and forecasting processes; partner closely with FP&A colleagues globally; drive continuous improvements to how they run and what they produce
  • Partner with senior leaders across trading desks and support functions to build and maintain annual budgets and rolling forecasts
  • Partner with global FP&A colleagues to align on planning timelines, methodology, and reporting standards
  • Extend financial planning capabilities toward longer-term strategic planning as the function matures

Cost Reporting & Expense Methodology

  • Own cost reporting across the firm; ensuring it is transparent, consistent, and directly relevant to business decisions
  • Maintain and improve cost driver definitions and allocation logic across trading desks, strategies, and support functions; document methodologies so they are auditable and easy to maintain
  • Develop and refine return metrics including return on capital and RWA, linking P&L performance to consumption at the desk and strategy level
  • Evaluate existing allocation approaches and simplify where they have become overly complex or inconsistent

Management Reporting

  • Own and continuously improve management reporting packages for senior leadership, covering cost performance vs. budget, capital efficiency metrics, and trend analysis
  • Make reporting easy to act on: senior leaders should read a package and know immediately where to focus
  • Build for scale; automated where possible, consistent with broader FP&A standards, and designed to grow with the business

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Serve as a finance partner to senior leaders across trading and support functions; turn complex financial data into clear, actionable takeaways
  • Partner with global FP&A colleagues to share best practices, align on governance standards, and ensure consistency across regions
  • Collaborate with Technology and Operations to improve data flows and underlying systems supporting FP&A
  • Handle ad hoc analytical requests from senior leadership quickly and accurately

Team Leadership & Development

  • Lead and develop the FP&A team day-to-day, setting clear priorities and creating an environment where people do their best work
  • Coach team members actively; providing regular feedback, investing in their development, and helping them grow into broader responsibilities over time
  • As the function scales, play a key role in building out the team: defining roles, supporting hiring, and onboarding new members effectively
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement, intellectual curiosity, and high standards for analytical rigor and communication

What we're looking for

  • 12+ years in FP&A or a comparable analytical finance role, ideally in financial services or a trading environment.
  • Demonstrated track record of improving FP&A capabilities — not just running existing processes.
  • Experience developing or refining expense methodologies and cost allocation frameworks.
  • Familiarity with return on capital, RWA, and P&L-relative cost metrics in a trading or financial services context.
  • Strong Excel skills; experience with BI and data tools such as Power BI, Tableau, and/or SQL.
  • Clear communicator who can build alignment across teams on complex financial topics.
  • Self-starter who takes ownership and is comfortable driving process improvement, including automation.
  • Experience building or managing a finance team is a plus.

Our Culture  

Our culture is anchored in excellence, meaning constant improvement, and it is deeply tied to our mission. Because markets are objective, competitive, and getting smarter everyday, we need to keep rapidly improving to have any chance of beating them. Truth is our most essential tool for engaging with the markets and constantly improving because once you know what's true about your problems and opportunities, you can determine how to get better. Valuing truth means being transparent about your decision-making and mistakes, giving and receiving feedback with humility, and fighting for the best answers over hierarchy, ego, or self-interest. Operating this way is hard – it's only possible because we build meaning in our work and relationships. This meaning comes from the audacity of the mission, and the joy of working alongside people who make you a better version of yourself. The culture, like Bridgewater itself, is always evolving. In 1997 our founder Ray Dalio wrote down his lessons, starting with a Philosophy Statement which remains our foundation. This later evolved into a set of 300+ Principles. In 2022, when Ray transitioned the company, we re-underwrote several of those principles and evolved others, with a specific focus on Meritocracy. Today the culture sits, alongside our people, as our most important edge. When we get it right, it’s the engine that powers everything else.

Collaboration: You will partner closely with our Infrastructure, Trading Desks, Project Management and Strategy Developer Teams to deliver and manage scalable and highly performant systems to support trading in the region and globally.

About Us

Wellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Our investment solutions, tailored to the unique return and risk objectives of institutional clients in more than 60 countries, draw on a robust body of proprietary research and a collaborative culture that encourages independent thought and healthy debate. As a private partnership, we believe our ownership structure fosters a long-term view that aligns our perspectives with those of our clients.

About the Role

THE POSITION 
We are looking for a Data Science Analyst (Science Analyst) to join the Healthcare team within Global Investment Research. With over $100B invested in healthcare, across over 50 Portfolio Managers, this represents a flagship franchise for Wellington. The Healthcare team invests globally across the full healthcare continuum, including Biopharma, Healthcare Services and Medical Technology. The Healthcare team includes over 10 colleagues.

The Science Analyst will work as an integral team member alongside Global Industry Analysts and Portfolio Managers, helping identify where data science, AI and alternative data can create differentiated investment insight across the healthcare sector (MedTech, Pharmaceuticals, Biotech, Healthcare Services). The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience in an investment setting, strong Python, SQL and AI skills, sound judgment for turning messy inputs into outputs the team can act on, and a genuine interest in the healthcare sector and the companies operating within it. They should be comfortable working independently, setting their own priorities, and moving fluidly between deep dataset work and quick-turnaround requests.

RESPONSIBILITIES
Responsibilities for this position will include the following:   

•    Work as an integral part of the Healthcare team, partnering directly with Global Industry Analysts and Portfolio Managers.
•    Translate broad investment questions into testable data science workflows and analytical outputs.
•    Apply AI and agentic tools to streamline research workflows and contribute directly to investment idea generation.
•    Communicate results clearly, including limitations, confidence levels, and interpretation risk.
•    Serve as an experienced data science resource across the Healthcare team's coverage areas.
•    Rapidly get up to speed on new companies, sub-sectors, datasets, and business models as the need arises.

  • Building and maintaining company financial models with a focus on product-level forecasting, procedure volumes, pricing, reimbursement, margin trends, and adoption curves;

Intellectual curiosity and a passion for understanding the drivers of MedTech, Tools and Diagnostics innovation are essential.

  • Judgment and investment focus – Successful candidates will demonstrate an ability to prioritize the most relevant information across a complex and fast-moving industry landscape and develop differentiated investment insights.   • Superior collaboration skills – The Research Associate will contribute meaningfully to the research efforts of the healthcare team while building strong working relationships across the firm. The ability to communicate investment views clearly, both verbally and in writing, and participate in a constructive investment dialogue is essential. 

  • Growth mindset – This role requires initiative, independence, and strong ownership of research responsibilities. The successful candidate will be proactive in identifying opportunities, deepening their expertise, and contributing to the team's investment process. 

 
QUALIFICATIONS

  • Understanding of long/short investing concepts and risk management approaches is beneficial;

  • High level of intellectual curiosity and willingness to engage deeply with clinical, technical, commercial, reimbursement, and financial material;

  • Strong data and technology skills, including experience using AI and tools to screen, rank, and analyze large stock universes;

Since 1971, our people have shaped our organization through a high-performance inclusive culture, in which we celebrate diverse thinking. We invest in our people and strive to imprint our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Responsibility and Excellence. We believe each of us is here to help others succeed and this has led to PIMCO being recognized as an innovator, industry thought leader and trusted advisor to our clients.

The Pricing Team is responsible for the day-to-day implementation of PIMCO’s Pricing Policy which describes the procedures and responsibilities related to the valuing of securities and other assets held in client portfolios, including registered funds, private funds, and separate accounts. The Pricing Team’s primary responsibility is the daily pricing of all the different asset types that PIMCO trades, including fixed income products like corporate bonds, municipal bonds, CMOs, and ABS, as well as complex derivatives related to swaps, options, FX, equities. To fulfill this responsibility, the team performs pricing accuracy testing, vendor comparisons, anomaly detection, price move research, and risk control functions to ensure that PIMCO’s assets are priced accurately and timely. The team primarily utilizes data from pricing vendors, including ICE Data Services, Bloomberg (BVAL), PricingDirect (PDI), S&P Global (Markit), and LSEG Data & Analytics (Refinitiv), among others, and interacts closely with these vendors on pricing challenges/inquiries, market updates, and technical support.

The Pricing Team interacts with many different internal and external teams, having to respond to a high volume of inquiries, including communicating with PIMCO’s Portfolio Managers to gain market insights/color and to help resolve pricing discrepancies. Other teams include the Valuation Team on Alternative Assets, Legal/Compliance, Risk/Analytics/Performance teams, Account Managers, Auditors, Clients, Fund Treasury team, Custodian Banks/Fund Admins, Index/Benchmark team, Asset Set Up/Security Master, Due Diligence/Enterprise risk teams, our back office service provider, and Technology teams.

In addition to conducting its daily operations related to pricing, the Pricing Team regularly presents valuation matters to the Pricing Committee and related Sub-Committees, as well as presenting to the Valuation Oversight Committees related to PIMCO’s 40 Act Fund Boards.

Core Responsibilities:

  • Daily security price validation by researching and resolving discrepancies as it relates to fixed income, derivatives, equity, ETF, FX, and commodity prices
  • Monitor, execute, enhance, and create new daily price quality assurance checks
  • Answer pricing related inquiries from internal and external stakeholders, including interaction with front office Portfolio Management team, pricing vendors, and Custodian banks
  • Conduct security pricing reviews related to financial audits
  • Assist in managing service providers that provide daily support functions related to daily production activities related to pricing securities
  • Create new and enhance existing workflows related to pricing responsibilities
  • Write business requirements for the technology teams to enhance our pricing applications

Position Requirements:

  • Minimum of a Bachelor’s Degree, preferably in Economics or Finance; MBA/CFA or in program is a plus
  • Relevant professional work experience within the financial services industry
  • Familiarity with basic fixed income products is recommended, but experience with complex derivatives (e.g. caps/floors, commodity index swaps/forwards, FX options/swaps, forward rate agreements, interest rate swaps/swaptions, total return swaps) is strongly preferred.
  • Experience with pricing vendors, PM/trading desk engagement, Bloomberg terminal, and fund audits is preferred
  • Strong technology skills, including proficiency in SQL, Python, and MS Excel is preferred
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work well in a team environment

PIMCO follows a total compensation approach when rewarding employees which includes a base salary and a discretionary bonus. Base salary is the fixed component of compensation that is determined by core job responsibilities, relevant experience, internal level, and market factors. The discretionary bonus is used to award performance and therefore is determined by company, business, team, and individual performance.

complex products and alternatives, as well as corporate action oversight in conjunction with outsourced providers.   • Conduct original research and develop systematic investment strategies across all asset classes, including equities, rates, commodities, credit, and FX.

  • Generate and test new research ideas using financial intuition, statistical learning, and large, diverse datasets.

  • Build and improve research infrastructure, including data pipelines, signal analytics, backtesting tools, and portfolio analytics.

  • Analyze strategy performance with attention to robustness, implementation, transaction costs, liquidity, and risk exposures.

  • Research opportunities across futures, forwards, options, swaps, and cash instruments, including relative value, directional, and cross-asset themes.

  • Experience working with large financial datasets, market data, and reproducible research workflows.

  • Ability to build clean, scalable research code and evaluate models rigorously.

About Bridgewater

Bridgewater Associates is a premier asset management firm, focused on delivering unique insight and partnership for the most sophisticated global institutional investors.

Our investment process is driven by a tireless pursuit to understand how the world’s markets and economies work — using cutting-edge technology to validate and execute on timeless and universal investment principles.

Founded in 1975, we are a community of independent thinkers who share a commitment for excellence. By fostering a culture of openness, transparency, and inclusion, we strive to unlock the most complex questions in investment strategy, management, and corporate culture.

Explore more information about Bridgewater on our website here.

Our Culture

Our culture is anchored in excellence, meaning constant improvement, and it is deeply tied to our mission. Because markets are objective, competitive, and getting smarter everyday, we need to keep rapidly improving to have any chance of beating them. Truth is our most essential tool for engaging with the markets and constantly improving because once you know what's true about your problems and opportunities, you can determine how to get better. Valuing truth means being transparent about your decision-making and mistakes, giving and receiving feedback with humility, and fighting for the best answers over hierarchy, ego, or self-interest. Operating this way is hard – it's only possible because we build meaning in our work and relationships. This meaning comes from the audacity of the mission, and the joy of working alongside people who make you a better version of yourself. The culture, like Bridgewater itself, is always evolving. In 1997 our founder Ray Dalio wrote down his lessons, starting with a Philosophy Statement which remains our foundation. This later evolved into a set of 300+ Principles. In 2022, when Ray transitioned the company, we re-underwrote several of those principles and evolved others, with a specific focus on Meritocracy. Today the culture sits, alongside our people, as our most important edge. When we get it right, it’s the engine that powers everything else.

About the Client Service Department

The goal of Client Service is to build and grow meaningful relationships with the world’s largest, most sophisticated investors and help clients achieve their goals through high quality return streams and tailored insights. To this end, we deeply understand the global pools of capital, develop strategies to effectively develop relationships, and partner with clients on their most difficult investment and portfolio construction problems. We help our clients broaden their understanding of our investment process, strategies and performance as well as deepen their understanding of financial markets more generally.

Overview

We're looking for a Site Reliability Engineer to keep the trading platforms we depend on healthy, performant and continuously improving. You'll operate within a set of platforms that span Windows and Linux: a distributed platform built on Service Fabric, real-time news infrastructure, and a large Python production environment, running across development, integration, and production in multiple regions. When something breaks you'll dive in, diagnose quickly, and fix it - then make the change that stops it happening again.

This is a hands-on engineering role that sits at the boundary between development and infrastructure. The team is evolving into reliability engineering: automation-first, monitoring-as-code, self-healing systems, and shared tooling built to production standard. You'll work in a tight-knit, business-facing team alongside developers, production and infrastructure engineers in Dublin, and partner closely with global platform-engineering teams - consuming their products and contributing to them upstream rather than building regional one-offs.

In this role you will:

OPERATE    Help run the production estate day to day: deployments, platform operations, capacity, certificates, and health checks across environments and tenants. Triage and resolve incidents quickly, perform root-cause analysis, and drive the permanent fix so the same problem doesn't come back.

About this role

Associate, Treasury (PFS)

 

Company Description

HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock, is a leading global, credit-focused alternative investment manager that seeks to provide creative capital solutions and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our clients. We manage various strategies across the capital structure, including privately negotiated senior debt; privately negotiated junior capital solutions in debt, preferred and equity formats; liquid credit including syndicated leveraged loans, collateralized loan obligations and high yield bonds; asset-based finance and real estate. The scale and breadth of our platform offers the flexibility to invest in companies large and small, through standard or customized solutions. At our core, we share a common thread of intellectual rigor and discipline that enables us to create value for our clients.

HPS was established in 2007 as a unit of Highbridge Capital Management, LLC (“HCM”), a subsidiary of JPMorgan Asset Management (“JPMAM”). On March 31, 2016, the senior executives of HPS acquired HPS and its subsidiaries from JPMAM and HCM (the “Transaction”.[i] Following the Transaction, JPMAM retained a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently redeemed in April 2022. In June 2018, affiliates of Dyal Capital Partners made a passive minority investment in HPS. In February 2022, an affiliate of The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America made a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently increased in August 2024. On July 1, 2025, BlackRock acquired the business and assets of HPS, with 100% of consideration paid in BlackRock equity (the “HPS/BlackRock Transaction”).

The HPS/BlackRock Transaction brings together BlackRock’s corporate and asset owner relationships with HPS’s diversified origination and capital flexibility. BlackRock and HPS have formed a new private financing solutions business unit (“PFS”) led by Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson, creating an integrated franchise with approximately $370 billion in client assets, including $205 billion of private credit assets.[ii] This combined platform, which has more than 590 investment professionals and approximately 1,300 employees globally,[iii] offers broad capabilities across senior and junior credit solutions, asset-based finance, real estate, CLOs and GP-LP solutions. As part of the HPS/BlackRock Transaction, Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson have joined BlackRock’s Global Executive Committee, and Scott Kapnick has been appointed as an observer to the BlackRock Board.

Department Description 

The Treasury team sources and negotiates bespoke financing for Illiquid Private Credit investments (aka Single Asset Financing). They are also responsible for mitigating the impact of currency and interest rate volatility on investments, overseeing all currency, interest rate hedging, and ensuring compliance with regulatory obligations. The Treasury team works closely with Investment teams, Deal Execution, Fund Accounting and Fund Finance teams to ensure liquidity management and optimization of resources.

 

Position Description

                                                 

HPS is currently seeking to recruit an Associate level candidate to join the Treasury team in New York to support the PFS platform. The role will include operational support for credit trading activity.

Responsibilities                                                                                                            

Specific responsibilities will include but not be limited to the following:

  • Reporting to the Head of Treasury and assisting in coordination of activities across the team.

  • Support portfolio liquidity reporting for Public Credit Trading Funds involving Prime Brokerage, Loan Facilities and structured financing vehicles.

  • Fulfill ISDA and bespoke financing reporting requirements.

  • Provide operational support for credit trading activity.

  • Assist AML-KYC onboarding and required documentation of new fund launches.

  • Resolve trade-related problems such as trade breaks, allocation and settlement issues.

  • Liaise with various counterparties on treasury issues impacting the Fund’s investment portfolio.

  • Support daily position reconciliation, trade settlement and valuation of traded hedge assets.

  • Maintain data integrity of internal trade capture, risk, and performance reporting systems.

  • Assist in ad-hoc projects (Treasury Management System Onboarding, Exposure Reporting, etc.)

Company Description

HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock, is a leading global, credit-focused alternative investment manager that seeks to provide creative capital solutions and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our clients. We manage various strategies across the capital structure, including privately negotiated senior debt; privately negotiated junior capital solutions in debt, preferred and equity formats; liquid credit including syndicated leveraged loans, collateralized loan obligations and high yield bonds; asset-based finance and real estate. The scale and breadth of our platform offers the flexibility to invest in companies large and small, through standard or customized solutions. At our core, we share a common thread of intellectual rigor and discipline that enables us to create value for our clients.
 

HPS was established in 2007 as a unit of Highbridge Capital Management, LLC (“HCM”), a subsidiary of JPMorgan Asset Management (“JPMAM”). On March 31, 2016, the senior executives of HPS acquired HPS and its subsidiaries from JPMAM and HCM (the “Transaction”.[i] Following the Transaction, JPMAM retained a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently redeemed in April 2022. In June 2018, affiliates of Dyal Capital Partners made a passive minority investment in HPS. In February 2022, an affiliate of The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America made a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently increased in August 2024. On July 1, 2025, BlackRock acquired the business and assets of HPS, with 100% of consideration paid in BlackRock equity (the “HPS/BlackRock Transaction”).
 

The HPS/BlackRock Transaction brings together BlackRock’s corporate and asset owner relationships with HPS’s diversified origination and capital flexibility. BlackRock and HPS have formed a new private financing solutions business unit (“PFS”) led by Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson, creating an integrated franchise with approximately $370 billion in client assets, including $205 billion of private credit assets.[ii] This combined platform, which has more than 590 investment professionals and approximately 1,300 employees globally,[iii] offers broad capabilities across senior and junior credit solutions, asset-based finance, real estate, CLOs and GP-LP solutions. As part of the HPS/BlackRock Transaction, Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson have joined BlackRock’s Global Executive Committee, and Scott Kapnick has been appointed as an observer to the BlackRock Board.
 

Department Description 

The Treasury team sources and negotiates bespoke financing for Illiquid Private Credit investments (aka Single Asset Financing). They are also responsible for mitigating the impact of currency and interest rate volatility on investments, overseeing all currency, interest rate hedging, and ensuring compliance with regulatory obligations. The Treasury team works closely with Investment teams, Deal Execution, Fund Accounting and Fund Finance teams to ensure liquidity management and optimization of resources.

  • Liaise with various counterparties on treasury issues impacting the Fund’s investment portfolio.

  • Support daily position reconciliation, trade settlement and valuation of traded hedge assets.

  • Maintain data integrity of internal trade capture, risk, and performance reporting systems.

About this role

Vice President, Investment Data Management (PFS)

Company Description

HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock, is a leading global, credit-focused alternative investment manager that seeks to provide creative capital solutions and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our clients. We manage various strategies across the capital structure, including privately negotiated senior debt; privately negotiated junior capital solutions in debt, preferred and equity formats; liquid credit including syndicated leveraged loans, collateralized loan obligations and high yield bonds; asset-based finance and real estate. The scale and breadth of our platform offers the flexibility to invest in companies large and small, through standard or customized solutions. At our core, we share a common thread of intellectual rigor and discipline that enables us to create value for our clients.

HPS was established in 2007 as a unit of Highbridge Capital Management, LLC (“HCM”), a subsidiary of JPMorgan Asset Management (“JPMAM”). On March 31, 2016, the senior executives of HPS acquired HPS and its subsidiaries from JPMAM and HCM (the “Transaction”. Following the Transaction, JPMAM retained a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently redeemed in April 2022. In June 2018, affiliates of Dyal Capital Partners made a passive minority investment in HPS. In February 2022, an affiliate of The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America made a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently increased in August 2024. On July 1, 2025, BlackRock acquired the business and assets of HPS, with 100% of consideration paid in BlackRock equity (the “HPS/BlackRock Transaction”).

The HPS/BlackRock Transaction brings together BlackRock’s corporate and asset owner relationships with HPS’s diversified origination and capital flexibility. BlackRock and HPS have formed a new private financing solutions business unit (“PFS”) led by Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson, creating an integrated franchise with approximately $370 billion in client assets, including $205 billion of private credit assets. This combined platform, which has more than 590 investment professionals and approximately 1,300 employees globally, offers broad capabilities across senior and junior credit solutions, asset-based finance, real estate, CLOs and GP-LP solutions. As part of the HPS/BlackRock Transaction, Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson have joined BlackRock’s Global Executive Committee, and Scott Kapnick has been appointed as an observer to the BlackRock Board.

Team Description:

The Investment Data Management team is responsible for the accurate and timely entry of all data-related items across the firm, as well as ensuring its proper flow and representation in downstream systems and reporting. The Investment Data Management team works closely with all elements of the firm, from the front office to ensure data is loaded correctly on initial set up, to back office to review the final data output, as well as infrastructure to assist in building out new processes to assist in daily workflow.

Position Description                                               
HPS is currently seeking a Vice President level candidate to join the Investment Data Management team based in New York, NY to support the PFS platform.  The individual should be highly organized with strong attention to detail. They should have the ability to meet strict deadlines, while working both independently and as part of a team. 

Responsibilities

Specific responsibilities will include but not be limited to the following:

  • Asset creation and maintenance across multiple asset classes (including but not limited to Bank Loans, Bonds, MBS/RMBS, Equities, Forwards, Options) in the firm’s Security Master

  • Analyze credit agreements on a daily basis

  • Reference data creation and maintenance in the firms Reference Master system

  • Maintain and monitor the data exception panel that reconciles vendor data feeds to internal data warehouse

  • Investigate & resolve any attribute discrepancies that may arise between data vendors internal systems

  • Daily interaction with Vendors, Risk, Technology, and Front Office teams to ensure proper creation of assets across the platform.

  • Creation and maintenance of internal strategies, UDF tags as well as clearing/executing broker accounts within firm systems

  • Mentor Junior people on the team.

  • Identify and implement process enhancements to the security master and related systems.

Candidate Profile

  • Graduate with a Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting or business related field

  • 6-10 years of experience in financial services industry, asset management preferred

  • Knowledge of bank loan products; Broadly Syndicated and Private

  • Proficient in Excel and Outlook

Prior to the Transaction, HPS was a subsidiary of HCM, which is a subsidiary of JPMAM, which in turn is a subsidiary of JPMorgan Chase & Co. (together with its affiliates, “JPM”). Immediately following the closing of the Transaction, the portfolio managers and other HPS employees responsible for the investment activities of HPS separated from JPM and continued to be employees of HPS. HPS is no longer deemed affiliated with JPM. AUM for PFS as of September 2, 2025. Note: Effective July 1, 2025, HPS became part of BlackRock. All AUM of June 30, 2025, except BlackRock non-CLO Leveraged Finance assets (as of August 2025). Represents pro forma combined AUM of HPS funds and BlackRock funds that form Private Financing Solutions (“PFS”) as of June 30, 2025. AUM of heritage HPS private credit funds, related managed accounts and certain other closed-ended liquid credit funds represent capital commitments during such funds’ investment periods and, post such funds’ investment periods, the cost of investment or latest available net asset value (including fund-level leverage but in all cases capped at capital commitments). AUM of liquid credit open-ended funds and related managed accounts other than CLOs represent the latest available net asset value. AUM of CLOs and warehouses represent the par value of collateral assets and cash in the portfolio. AUM of business development companies represents net asset value plus leverage (inclusive of drawn and undrawn amounts) as of the prior month-end. AUM of ElmTree Funds represents the gross assets plus uncalled commitments over a fund’s life with the exception of ElmTree Unity Debt Fund, LP which represents total commitments of the fund. AUM strategy is assigned at the fund level based on target strategy allocations. The AUM for heritage BlackRock funds is calculated as follows: (i) for evergreen funds, commingled funds and mandates in their investment period: as the sum of fee-paying and any non-fee-paying client commitments, and the maximum permissible leverage for any levered vehicles; (ii) for commingled funds and mandates in runoff: as the aggregate of each fund's net asset value, any unfunded commitments to portfolio companies, and drawn leverage as of the reporting date, if any; and (iii) for semi-liquid funds: as the aggregate of each fund's net asset value. In all cases, AUM is inclusive of internal BlackRock allocations. The AUM figures are presented in US dollars. Effective July 1, 2025, HPS became part of BlackRock. Effective September 2, 2025, Elm Tree Funds became part of BLK and is included within HPS funds. Headcount as of date varies given recent closings of transactions.

MASS constructs active asset allocation strategies and whole portfolio solutions across a wide spectrum of commingled funds, separate accounts, model portfolios, and outsourcing solutions in the wealth and institutional channels. Currently, MASS handles over $1 trillion in assets and has a strong presence in the United States, Europe, and Asia Pacific.

Company Description

HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock, is a leading global, credit-focused alternative investment manager that seeks to provide creative capital solutions and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our clients. We manage various strategies across the capital structure, including privately negotiated senior debt; privately negotiated junior capital solutions in debt, preferred and equity formats; liquid credit including syndicated leveraged loans, collateralized loan obligations and high yield bonds; asset-based finance and real estate. The scale and breadth of our platform offers the flexibility to invest in companies large and small, through standard or customized solutions. At our core, we share a common thread of intellectual rigor and discipline that enables us to create value for our clients.

HPS was established in 2007 as a unit of Highbridge Capital Management, LLC (“HCM”), a subsidiary of JPMorgan Asset Management (“JPMAM”). On March 31, 2016, the senior executives of HPS acquired HPS and its subsidiaries from JPMAM and HCM (the “Transaction”).[i] Following the Transaction, JPMAM retained a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently redeemed in April 2022. In June 2018, affiliates of Dyal Capital Partners made a passive minority investment in HPS. In February 2022, an affiliate of The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America made a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently increased in August 2024. On July 1, 2025, BlackRock acquired the business and assets of HPS, with 100% of consideration paid in BlackRock equity (the “HPS/BlackRock Transaction”).

The HPS/BlackRock Transaction brings together BlackRock’s corporate and asset owner relationships with HPS’s diversified origination and capital flexibility. BlackRock and HPS have formed a new private financing solutions business unit (“PFS”) led by Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson, creating an integrated franchise with approximately $370 billion in client assets, including $205 billion of private credit assets.[ii] This combined platform, which has more than 590 investment professionals and approximately 1,300 employees globally,[iii] offers broad capabilities across senior and junior credit solutions, asset-based finance, real estate, CLOs and GP-LP solutions. As part of the HPS/BlackRock Transaction, Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson have joined BlackRock’s Global Executive Committee, and Scott Kapnick has been appointed as an observer to the BlackRock Board.

The Middle Office team (MO) within Private Financing Solutions (PFS) – Blackrock’s private credit platform – is responsible for ensuring the Fund’s positions and cash balances are accurate. MO handles ad-hoc requests that come from the deal team and/or separately managed account clients. Job Description 

We are seeking a Vice President, Identity Security Engineer to help shape and deliver a major identity modernisation programme, migrating from SailPoint IdentityIQ to SailPoint Identity Security Cloud. This is a hands-on technical leadership role for an engineer who enjoys solving complex security, data, integration and operating-model challenges at enterprise scale. You will work with engineering, security, operations and business partners to design a modern identity platform that is secure, resilient, scalable and easier for people to use. The successful candidate will combine deep SailPoint and identity governance expertise with the judgement, ownership and communication skills needed to lead complex changes across a global organisation. 

Key Responsibilities 

  • Lead the technical design and delivery of the migration from SailPoint IdentityIQ to SailPoint Identity Security Cloud, treating the move as a platform transformation rather than a like-for-like upgrade. 

  • Define the future-state identity architecture, including identity data models, application onboarding patterns, access request processes, provisioning, deprovisioning, certifications and policy controls. 

  • Translate complex IdentityIQ workflows, rules, connectors and customisations into secure, maintainable, cloud-aligned designs using Identity Security Cloud capabilities and extensibility options. 

  • Make practical engineering decisions that balance security, user experience, delivery risk, regulatory expectations and long-term maintainability. 

  • Partner with application, infrastructure, cloud, HR, operations, risk and compliance teams to resolve dependencies and keep delivery moving across a complex enterprise environment. 

  • Lead technical planning across discovery, design, build, testing, parallel run, cutover and operational readiness, with clear ownership of risks, dependencies and outcomes. 

  • Set high engineering standards for documentation, testing, observability, change control, resilience and secure-by-design delivery. 

  • Coach engineers, share technical knowledge and create an environment where teams can make good decisions quickly and safely. 

  • Identify opportunities to simplify legacy processes, reduce manual effort, improve controls and unlock the benefits of a modern cloud identity platform. 

Qualifications / Competencies 

  • Strong hands-on experience designing, building or leading SailPoint IdentityIQ, SailPoint Identity Security Cloud, or comparable identity governance platforms. 

  • Experience with IdentityIQ to Identity Security Cloud migration, cloud identity transformation, or modernisation of a mature identity governance environment. 

  • Deep understanding of identity governance and administration, including joiner, mover and leaver processes, access requests, certifications, role models, policies and segregation of duties. 

  • Ability to assess existing workflows, rules, connectors, data flows and customisations, then redesign them for a more scalable and maintainable cloud platform. 

  • Strong engineering background across APIs, integrations, directories, HR sources, application onboarding, automation and secure system design. 

  • Experience integrating identity platforms with Microsoft Entra ID, Active Directory, LDAP, HR systems, SaaS applications, on-premises applications and privileged access platforms. 

  • Comfortable leading technical discussions with senior stakeholders and explaining complex engineering trade-offs in clear, practical language. 

  • Proven ability to lead complex initiatives across distributed teams, manage ambiguity and drive delivery without losing sight of quality or risk. 

  • Strong ownership mindset, with the ability to anticipate problems, remove blockers and make decisions that move the programme forward. 

  • Clear communicator who can build trust with engineering teams, business partners and control functions. 

 

Desirable Skills 

  • SailPoint certification, Identity Security Cloud Engineer certification, CISSP, CISM or similar security qualification. 

  • Experience using identity analytics, risk-based access insights or AI-assisted governance to improve access decisions and reduce manual review effort. 

  • Experience with CyberArk or other privileged access management technologies. 

  • Experience delivering security or identity change in regulated, high-scale or highly governed environments. 

  • Understanding of Zero Trust, least privilege, non-human identities, cloud security and modern access governance patterns. 

  • Experience simplifying legacy processes and helping teams adopt more modern engineering practices.

Company Description

HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock, is a leading global, credit-focused alternative investment manager that seeks to provide creative capital solutions and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our clients. We manage various strategies across the capital structure, including privately negotiated senior debt; privately negotiated junior capital solutions in debt, preferred and equity formats; liquid credit including syndicated leveraged loans, collateralized loan obligations and high yield bonds; asset-based finance and real estate. The scale and breadth of our platform offers the flexibility to invest in companies large and small, through standard or customized solutions. At our core, we share a common thread of intellectual rigor and discipline that enables us to create value for our clients.

HPS was established in 2007 as a unit of Highbridge Capital Management, LLC (“HCM”), a subsidiary of JPMorgan Asset Management (“JPMAM”). On March 31, 2016, the senior executives of HPS acquired HPS and its subsidiaries from JPMAM and HCM (the “Transaction”.[i] Following the Transaction, JPMAM retained a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently redeemed in April 2022. In June 2018, affiliates of Dyal Capital Partners made a passive minority investment in HPS. In February 2022, an affiliate of The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America made a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently increased in August 2024. On July 1, 2025, BlackRock acquired the business and assets of HPS, with 100% of consideration paid in BlackRock equity (the “HPS/BlackRock Transaction”).

The HPS/BlackRock Transaction brings together BlackRock’s corporate and asset owner relationships with HPS’s diversified origination and capital flexibility. BlackRock and HPS have formed a new private financing solutions business unit (“PFS”) led by Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson, creating an integrated franchise with approximately $370 billion in client assets, including $205 billion of private credit assets.[ii] This combined platform, which has more than 590 investment professionals and approximately 1,300 employees globally,[iii] offers broad capabilities across senior and junior credit solutions, asset-based finance, real estate, CLOs and GP-LP solutions. As part of the HPS/BlackRock Transaction, Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson have joined BlackRock’s Global Executive Committee, and Scott Kapnick has been appointed as an observer to the BlackRock Board.

About this role

Responsible for driving overall product strategy, as well related strategic initiatives to evolve the platform in response to client (internal and external) needs in order to increase revenue opportunity for the firm.  Partners with investment team, users, technology leaders and other stakeholders (e.g., sales, marketing, engineers) to shape vision for the next “version” of the platform and define the overall deployment strategy.  Innovates, conceptualizes, designs and pilots new capabilities available. Also sets in place process and framework for continuous improvement of platform to enhance stability, reliability and performance.

Veterans Transition Program-Technical Relationship Manager, Aladdin – Associate

We recognize that veterans bring a unique and valued perspective to BlackRock thanks to their extraordinary backgrounds and experiences.  The Veterans Transition Program is designed to support veterans in making the transition from military life to the civilian workforce. The Program offers participants the opportunity to work at the world’s largest asset manager for six months. On completion of the Program, successful participants will be offered permanent employment at BlackRock.

Over the course of the Program, participants will:

  • Join teams and have an immediate impact;

  • Immerse themselves in the work of their teams;

  • Gain an understanding of how BlackRock serves its clients;

  • Be supported through training and mentorship;

  • Get exposure to senior leaders;

  • Participate in social and networking opportunities.

Program Structure:

The program begins with an orientation where you’ll learn about BlackRock’s principles, mission, purpose, and culture. You’ll learn about the asset management industry and get an in-depth look at how BlackRock serves its clients.  Following orientation, you’ll join your team and gain insights into the day-to-day life of an Associate as you develop subject-matter expertise through on-the-job learning and our industry-leading technology, Aladdin.

Aladdin® is an operating system for investment managers that seeks to connect the information, people, and technology needed to manage money in real time. The Aladdin platform combines risk analytics with portfolio management, trading, compliance, and operations tools on a single platform to power informed decision-making, effective risk management, efficient trading, and operational scale. Aladdin is used by a community of over 200 institutional clients around the world, including BlackRock. There are over 50,000 end users of Aladdin globally. The team is comprised of 800+ professionals responsible for implementing and supporting our Aladdin clients, sales and marketing, and ensuring the Aladdin Community maximizes Aladdin products through engagement and education.

We are seeking an Aladdin Technical Relationship Manager to work closely with Aladdin clients to be their trusted consultant, problem solver, and business partner – and to take full advantage of Aladdin.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Own relationships with client teams and help them use Aladdin to achieve their firm’s goals 

  • Able to map Aladdin Product vision across a client’s business / strategic initiative and articulate the value.

  • Understands client’s Aladdin adoption and develops a strategy for approaching clients on product & harvesting opportunities. 

  • Acts as a consultative partner to senior client stakeholders, providing product insights

  • Demonstrates strong segment and industry knowledge; accountable for multiple user segments / clients.

  • Apply deep client and technical expertise to shape regional themes and identifies risks and opportunities.

  • Ensure client feedback on product is communicated to the Product Managers and is tracked through successful development and deployment. 

  • Keep updated on regulatory and operational industry trends to help your clients stay ahead of changing times
